narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.persona: a patient, precise instructor who counts out loud, demonstrates from the front and the back, repeats every step slowly three times before speeding up, names mistakes kindly and never rushes
instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

scenes.title: Cold open
narration: Originating in 1930s Australia, New Vogue sequence dances always run for exactly 16 or 32 bars, making them uniquely approachable for beginners.
This is New Vogue. 1930s.
on_screen: Hero video, first 10 seconds (4RldSmDzb9Y)

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The New Vogue dance style is an Australian form of ballroom sequence dancing that originated in the 1930s.
It has since become an important part in the Australian and New Zealand ballroom scene and is one of the three Dancesport styles in Australia, alongside traditional Ballroom and Latin American.
on_screen: Map: Australia · Oceania
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Since 2019 the Services Club in Canowindra, NSW, hosts in late June a 12-hour event that features only Australian New Vogue Dances to live music, attracting participants from all over Australia.
They are competed in recreational, amateur, professional, ability dance/special dance, vision impaired dance, and para dance divisions.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: All New Vogue dances are based on a sequence of dance steps which are continually repeated, usually until the music ends.
These sequences are always either 16 or 32 bars long.
Higher levels require more precise steps and the addition of arm and torso movement, known as styling.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: New Vogue dances require music that is in turn sequenced, composed of verses that are either 16 or 32 bars long.
The dances are based on sub categories including Viennese Waltz Rhythm, Slow Foxtrot Rhythm, March Rhythm and Tango Rhythm.

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
